tooling.capture_driver: UNKNOWN - no HTTP client was recorded at capture time; the earlier value naming python3 urllib.request was supplied by envelope normalisation, was never observed, and is corrected to UNKNOWN - see _capture.notes and HARVEST-MANIFEST.md section 3.3.1

notes: FACT: `. /etc/profile.d/blitzy-cobolcheck-env.sh` was issued as the literal first command of this run; the script is present in this container and sourcing returned rc=0. This capture requires only `curl` and `python3`, both already on PATH, so no finding, amendment request or UNKNOWN label follows from the activation step either way.

FACT: `authenticated` was derived solely from the observed rate-limit ceiling x-ratelimit-limit=5000 on GET https://api.github.com/rate_limit (corroborated by resources.core.limit=5000), where 5000 denotes an authenticated quota and 60 an unauthenticated one; it was not derived from the presence of any token variable.
FACT: the comments endpoint returned HTTP 200 with zero records, so `issue_comments` is an empty array; this is a complete capture of an empty thread rather than a failed capture.
FACT: pagination followed the Link rel="next" header until it was absent; the final comments page recorded link_next=null, so 1 page(s) exhausted the thread and 0 comment record(s) were captured.
FACT: every captured body is stored verbatim as returned by the API — no field was pruned or truncated, no markdown was re-rendered, no HTML was stripped and no whitespace was normalized.

FACT: the retrieved issue payload reports comments=0, which matches the 0 record(s) captured into `issue_comments`; the API's own comment counter is therefore an independent check that this capture is complete rather than silently truncated.

FACT: every entry in `_capture.calls` records method "GET"; no POST, PATCH, PUT or DELETE request was issued, and no comment, reaction, label, assignment, reopen or edit was attempted against the archived read-only repository openmainframeproject/cobol-check.

UNKNOWN: CREDENTIAL TRANSPORT EXPOSURE — `FACT` — the capture for this artifact recorded no HTTP client field at all: its `_capture.tooling` held only observed tool versions and the nothing-installed posture, and the `capture_driver` value naming python3 `urllib.request` was supplied later by envelope normalisation rather than observed. `UNKNOWN` — which client issued these requests is not recoverable after the fact, so `capture_driver` is corrected to an explicit `UNKNOWN` and the exposure is classified `UNKNOWN` at `_capture.credential_transport_exposure` instead of asserting an unobserved value. What IS established: no credential value, header or fragment appears anywhere in this artifact at rest, and every call in `_capture.calls` is a `GET`. The transport rule binding any future authenticated capture is fixed in `upstream-harvest/HARVEST-MANIFEST.md` section 3.3.1.

FACT: PUBLIC-DATA GOVERNANCE — this artifact retains public GitHub records verbatim, including contributor `login`, profile and avatar URLs, timestamps and comment bodies, because it is the audit copy of a one-time capture against an archived repository and fidelity is its purpose. Use of that data is bounded to backlog triage and provenance audit for this programme. The binding purpose, access and publication boundary, retention trigger, disposal rule, deleted-upstream-content handling and the prohibition on profiling, enrichment, outreach and every other secondary use are stated in `upstream-harvest/HARVEST-MANIFEST.md` section 12. Those rules constrain use and lifetime; they never license editing this evidence.

FACT: ZERO-RECORD CORROBORATION — `issue_comments` holds zero records because the thread is genuinely empty, not because a page was lost or a body was silently truncated. Locator: `_capture.calls[1]` records GET https://api.github.com/repos/openmainframeproject/cobol-check/issues/53/comments?per_page=100 at http_status = 200 with records_returned = 0, records_persisted = 0 and link_next = null, and the retained `issue` payload at `issue.comments` carries 0 — GitHub's own counter for the same thread. INFERENCE: the zero is corroborated by a value this capture did not choose; reasoning: the counter is computed upstream and travels in a different payload, so an empty array and a zero counter agreeing is independent evidence rather than a restatement of the same observation. FACT: this classification is required rather than optional — `capture-envelope.schema.json` at envelope_schema_version 1.2.0 invariant C5 makes an unclassified zero-record data family invalid, because a genuinely empty thread and a truncated page otherwise produce byte-identical artifacts.
